title: Class template argument deduction (CTAD) and deduction guides
recap: CTAD uses initialization arguments to deduce class template arguments. A deduction guide specifies how argument types map to a specialization; it is not a function body.
Deducing a common type for mixed numeric arguments prevents accidental truncation. The resulting object must really store that type, not merely cast during a later calculation.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice class template argument deduction (ctad) and deduction guides.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Add a deduction guide so Pair{left,right} deduces Pair<std::common_type_t<T,U>> from possibly mixed numeric arguments. Then implement spanOf(pair), returning the absolute difference of its two members as T. Pair{2,5.5} must store two doubles, not truncate. std::common_type_t is provided by <type_traits>; it names the common arithmetic type. Inputs and differences fit their types.
hints: The guide begins template <typename T, typename U>.
Compute a nonnegative difference using the stored member type.
